summary: The plan editor's outdoor-only site kind gains four new object types - Road, Tree, Hedge and Ground - each declared entirely in the P3 object registry (`components/map/plan_objects.js`): a `draw2d` hook for the editor canvas, an `svg2d` hook for the read-only floor view, and a `build3d` hook for the three.js scene, so none of the three JS renderers needed a per-type edit to gain them (the 3D scene grew three reusable primitives - a flat area, an extruded ribbon, a tree - instead of four bespoke builders). A Road is a polyline centreline with a width (metres), surface (asphalt/concrete/gravel/paved) and lane markings, deliberately never stored in `segments` (those extrude into full-height walls, which would turn a road into a wall down the middle of the site). A Tree is a point with a canopy radius, a height and a clear stem - the field that decides whether a camera mounted below the canopy can see past it. A Hedge is a polyline with its own width/height, the low solid occluder that actually blocks a fence-line camera, kept separate from a wall so an operator hiding/erasing a hedge never touches a wall. Ground is a closed, painted-first polygon (grass/water/gravel/hardstanding) that makes a site plan read as a site rather than a diagram of fences. The floor model version bumps to 3; these tools appear only on outdoor sites, since a road inside a building is a category error. The Go PDF compositor (`report_floorgrid.go`) was taught all four via a new `scale float64` parameter threaded from `reports.go`/`report_floorplan.go` (the outdoor kit's fields are real-world metres, unlike every other array which is image pixels), plus a polygon scanline fill and circle rasterisers; the frontend/Go parity test (`report_floorgrid_parity_test.go`) failed by name until this landed, exactly as it was built to. Building this also caught a real UI defect: the properties inspector showed two controls both labelled "Width" for a road (its own carriageway width, and the transform block's unrelated bounding-box width); the type's own field now wins and the colliding bounding-box control is dropped, compared on the rendered label so the fix holds in every language. Four new glyphs (road/hedge/tree/ground) were added to the shared icon set (`frontend/shared/src/icons.js`), and 35 new i18n keys were added per language (en/ms/zh/ar). This is phase P5 ("the outdoor kit") of docs/MYSELIASAN_PLAN_EDITOR_PLAN.md.
compatibility: Frontend + Go PDF compositor change, no schema/config change. Existing installs get the four new tools automatically on the next build/deploy, offered only on sites already marked `outdoor` - a building site's toolset and editor are completely unaffected. An existing floor's saved `Grid` JSON (model v2 or earlier) opens unchanged; the new arrays are simply absent until an operator draws something with the new tools, and an older build reading a v3 model keeps the roads/trees/hedges/ground arrays it does not recognise verbatim (the same forward-compatible round-trip `readModel`/`writeModel` already provided for P1-P4). The Go PDF report signature change (`renderFloorPlacements`/`renderFloorGrid` now take the floor's scale) is internal to `apps/myseliasan/services`; no API contract changes, and a plan that has never had its scale set still renders correctly via the same nominal 0.5 m/cell fallback the editor already used.
